steps.title: An open E minor shape
steps.body:
**open chord** means a chord shape that includes at least one open string. Em is a short way to write E minor. Its notes are E, G and B; several strings repeat those names. In the picture, 0 means open, a dot shows a fret to press, and x means leave that string out.

**Why it matters:** Open strings let you play a full chord with only a few pressed positions.

steps.title: Read and hear the notes
steps.body: For Em, press fret 2 on strings 5 and 4. Leave strings 6, 3, 2 and 1 open. Tap the shown positions in the app. The check looks for the three note names, so a smaller correct version counts too.

items.prompt: Play E, B, E, G, B, E together. Use any positions for these notes.

steps.title: Make it familiar
steps.body: On your guitar, press lightly just behind each fret. Pluck the strings one at a time to hear clarity; in the app use taps rather than the single-note microphone for the chord check.

items.prompt: Play E, B, E, G, B, E together. Use any positions for these notes.
